title: The Ethylene Effect: Why Your Fruit Dies Next to Your Greens
editorialNotes: No PantryPal occurrence (Tier 1 CTA is anonymous); no swap.

copy.headline: Your fruit is killing your vegetables.
copy.body: And you're putting them in the same drawer.

copy.headline: Ethylene gas.
items: Apples, bananas, avocados, tomatoes, and peaches release a natural ripening gas as they age.
It's invisible and odorless. It accelerates spoilage in everything around them.
copy.citation: Source: USDA / UC Davis Postharvest Center

copy.headline: What it destroys.
copy.body: Leafy greens, broccoli, cauliflower, cucumbers, and carrots are ethylene-sensitive. Stored next to ethylene producers, they wilt and yellow 2–3x faster.

copy.headline: The crisper drawer fix.
items: If your fridge has two drawers:
Never mix them. One drawer of each.

copy.headline: The counter rule.
copy.body: Bananas on the counter ripen everything nearby. Keep them isolated. A banana hook isn't aesthetic — it's functional.

copy.headline: Separating ethylene producers from sensitive foods can extend produce life by 4–7 days. That's the difference between eating it and trashing it.
